fact: UN DESA states Irembo is Rwanda's national online service portal, born of a partnership between RwandaOnline Platform Ltd and the Government of Rwanda, in operation since 2015.
UN DESA states Irembo has grown to provide access to more than 90 government services online.

The Internet Society says a Karongi father renewed his family's health insurance and could request a marriage certificate copy through Rwanda's Irembo platform on his own phone, and that government initiatives are moving essential services online.
DIAL reports IremboGov is a one-stop portal for over 240 public services that citizens can access digitally and remotely.
The 13th Rwanda Governance Scorecard (RGB, 22 October 2026) reports satisfaction with Irembo, the government services platform, at 81.80%, down 5.60 points on the previous assessment.
The scorecard cites 2024 Ministry of ICT and Innovation data that only 11% of government services were fully digitised, letting users complete the process online without other channels.

The KT Press report on the Rwanda Governance Scorecard says citizens can apply for documents, pay fees and access public services through online platforms such as Irembo, and that 12 land services are online.

Minister Paula Ingabire told the Chamber of Deputies that the Irembo platform offers 240 government services, including civil registration, driving permits and business licences, which citizens can apply for online.
MINICT says citizens submitted over 5 million applications through Irembo between 2023 and 2024, and more than 400,000 Rwandans had opened personal accounts as of March 2025.
The deck says 247+ government services are available on Irembo, which is also the channel for Single Digital Identity pre-enrollment.
The Rwanda Development Board's guide says businesses log in with their IremboAccount to apply online for its business and investor services.
IremboGov says residents must log in to their Irembo account on irembo.gov.rw to apply for Single Digital ID pre-enrollment, listed under the portal's Identification category.
The ministry's sector plan says the Irembo e-government site, set up in 2014, has 56 e-services, with over 150 other online services not integrated into it.
The ministry's sector plan says Irembo runs a monthly transaction count of 1,445,186; it gives no date beyond 'to date', so the plan's November 2017 publication date is used.

The Smart City Rwanda Masterplan describes the Irembo e-government portal as an online platform where citizens can access more than 30 different government services in one place; it gives no date, so its 2017 publication year is used.
The master plan's baseline table puts the number of government services on the Irembo platform at 10, with 432 Irembo centres, for the 2014 baseline.
